main_text.p: tonis, Philosophiam suam vocat dif-ceptationem somnio non absimilem.

Pag. 15. l. 9. post termini, addantur ea, quæ sequuntur: Notandum siquidem, Socratis ævo, Sophistas regnasse, atque circa res naturales quam plurimum suam venditasse scientiam, somniantes se jam pervenisse ad interiora earum penetralia, cum circa umbras & cortices solum occuparentur: quos, ut Socrates & Plato contunderent, ea, quæ notata jam est, ratione illos aggredi instituerunt. Patet potissimum ex Hippia Majore, qui non nisi lusus esse videtur in Sophistas, ad eorum fastum retundendum institutus. Quod & innuit ipse Plato in Charmide sic loquens: Quæ nullo modo quis nescit, non potest cognoscere se ignorare, quæ insciitia supra fatuam Sophistarum ostentationem, quæ arguebatur a Socrate, posita est.

page.notes: The first line of the page is a fragment continuing from the previous text. The last line "quentia" is the continuation of "sequentia" split across the page. Some letters in the scan are faint (e.g. "Phi losophiam", "Sophistas") and were read with reasonable confidence; the word "Sophistas" in the first paragraph and "ab" in "absimilem" are slightly uncertain. Stain marks at the lower right corner were ignored.
